title: Agent Tool Contract Design Template
summary: Design model-callable tools with a narrow purpose, explicit schemas, enforced authorization, predictable errors, and verifiable side effects.
prerequisites: A bounded capability that should be exposed to an agent

sections.title: Design one observable capability
paragraphs: This complete worked case is synthetic. The reserve-study-room operation reserves one fictional room for one listed slot using in-memory dictionaries. It contacts no service, uses no network, writes no persistent state, and represents no real facility.

The untrusted model payload contains only requested_slot, request_id, and confirmation. Trusted identity, tenant, and permissions arrive separately as runtime context. The corrected boundary rejects model-supplied identity, caller, tenant, permissions, undeclared fields, unsupported slots, malformed identifiers, non-Boolean confirmation values, malformed context, and more than eight permissions before reading reservation or cache state.

JSON Schema draft 2020-12 supplies keywords such as type, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, pattern, and const. The Python validators in this exercise explicitly implement this particular contract. They are not claimed to be a complete JSON Schema implementation.

Authorization uses only validated runtime context and occurs before reservation or idempotency state is observed. The output statuses are success, denied, conflict, and pending. Success requires a verified in-memory postcondition. Pending means a simulated effect may have occurred but confirmation evidence is unavailable. It is never presented as success.

The idempotency key is the trusted tenant, trusted caller, and request_id. A SHA-256 digest additionally binds that key to the canonical accepted payload. An exact replay returns a deep copy of the cached receipt. Reusing the key with changed payload returns conflict. Reconciliation validates context, permission, payload, key, digest, and cached operation before one bounded state check. It never issues a second reservation attempt.

MCP annotations such as read-only, destructive, and idempotent are hints, not authorization or runtime enforcement. This local teaching contract is not a production MCP server. A production deployment still needs authenticated transport, server-supplied context, concurrency control, durable storage, monitoring, and deployment-specific recovery.
sections.callout:
Filled worked record:
Tool name and version: reserve-study-room 1.0.0. Purpose: reserve room-lantern for one supported slot. Use when a validated runtime caller has reserve:study-room and confirmation is exactly true. Do not use for cancellation, room creation, arbitrary scheduling, or real facilities. Input: requested_slot, request_id, confirmation, with no extra properties. Trusted context: identity, tenant, permissions. Output: success, denied, conflict, or pending plus operation ID, room, slot, bounded evidence, and a reason code with actionable feedback. Side effect: one in-memory dictionary entry. Risk hints: readOnly=false, destructive=false, idempotent=true, openWorld=false. Approval: exact permission and explicit confirmation. Retry rule: replay only an identical digest; changed payload conflicts. Recovery: inspect a matching pending operation at most once and never blindly repeat the effect. Precondition: validated input, validated context, permission, unused slot. Postcondition: success only when the room entry exactly matches trusted tenant and caller. Compensation: no automatic cancellation is implemented. Logging: safe IDs and reason codes may be retained; secrets are not accepted.

sections.title: Versioned output schema
paragraphs: The output schema makes failure feedback renderable through reason.code and reason.message. Evidence includes an exact Boolean and a reconciliation count bounded to zero or one. The explicit Python validator also enforces the cross-field rule that success requires reserved=true and every other status requires reserved=false.

sections.title: Record the complete tool contract
paragraphs: Save this complete standard-library implementation as reserve_room.py. json.dumps with sorted keys creates the canonical digest material, hashlib.sha256 hashes its UTF-8 bytes, re.fullmatch checks complete identifiers, and copy.deepcopy isolates nested cached evidence from caller mutation.

All public operations validate container and primitive types before indexing, membership tests, regular expressions, cache access, room access, or mutation. Rejections return controlled, schema-valid diagnostics. Invalid output produced through the explicitly named test seam causes rollback of rooms, cache, and sequence before POSTCONDITION_UNVERIFIED is returned.

The reconciliation limit is one observation for a pending operation. If that observation cannot confirm ownership, the receipt remains pending. Later calls return the bounded pending receipt without another state observation or mutation.

sections.title: Synthetic worked fixture
paragraphs: Save this complete local fixture as worked_fixture.json. The expected first operation is op-0001. It reserves room-lantern at 09:00Z for trusted tenant-cedar and user-ivy. Replaying the same fixture returns the same receipt and leaves exactly one room entry.

sections.title: Deliberately insecure schema-only authorization variant
paragraphs: This separate local variant is deliberately insecure. It validates a permissive payload shape and then trusts tenant supplied by that payload. It exists only to make the authorization flaw observable. It is not imported by the corrected implementation.

The contract tests independently prove two facts. First, the insecure variant mutates under tenant-maple when the payload supplies that tenant. Second, the corrected RoomService rejects the identical forged payload and preserves its rooms, cache, and sequence. The strict-schema regression separately calls validate_input with the forged payload, asserts ValueError, and verifies that the insecure service has not been mutated because the insecure service is never reached.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Save every labeled file separately in one local directory. Run these commands with Python 3: python3 reserve_room.py --demo worked, python3 reserve_room.py --demo changed, python3 test_contract.py, and python3 test_changed_solution.py. They require only the Python standard library, perform no downloads or remote writes, and need no provider account. The demo reads only the supplied local fixture. unittest provides the test-case and result mechanisms used here: https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html.

Expected worked demo output, shown as a synthetic deterministic expectation rather than a claim of execution: {"first": {"evidence": {"caller": "user-ivy", "reconciliation_count": 0, "reserved": true, "tenant": "tenant-cedar"}, "operation_id": "op-0001", "reason": {"code": "RESERVATION_CONFIRMED", "message": "reservation postcondition is confirmed"}, "room_id": "room-lantern", "slot": "2026-10-05T09:00Z", "status": "success"}, "replay": {"evidence": {"caller": "user-ivy", "reconciliation_count": 0, "reserved": true, "tenant": "tenant-cedar"}, "operation_id": "op-0001", "reason": {"code": "RESERVATION_CONFIRMED", "message": "reservation postcondition is confirmed"}, "room_id": "room-lantern", "slot": "2026-10-05T09:00Z", "status": "success"}, "state": {"room-lantern|2026-10-05T09:00Z": ["tenant-cedar", "user-ivy"]}}

Expected changed demo output, also a synthetic deterministic expectation: {"first": {"evidence": {"caller": "user-ivy", "reconciliation_count": 0, "reserved": true, "tenant": "tenant-maple"}, "operation_id": "op-0001", "reason": {"code": "RESERVATION_CONFIRMED", "message": "reservation postcondition is confirmed"}, "room_id": "room-lantern", "slot": "2026-10-05T10:00Z", "status": "success"}, "replay": {"evidence": {"caller": "user-ivy", "reconciliation_count": 0, "reserved": true, "tenant": "tenant-maple"}, "operation_id": "op-0001", "reason": {"code": "RESERVATION_CONFIRMED", "message": "reservation postcondition is confirmed"}, "room_id": "room-lantern", "slot": "2026-10-05T10:00Z", "status": "success"}, "state": {"room-lantern|2026-10-05T10:00Z": ["tenant-maple", "user-ivy"]}}

The main test runner has eight contract tests. The deterministic expected result is eight PASS lines followed by SUMMARY tests=8 passed=8 failures=0 errors=0. This is an expected output, not a claim that the tests were executed while drafting. The strict-schema regression is a passing test: it expects ValueError from validate_input for the injected tenant and then verifies that the insecure service state remains unchanged.

The negative cases cover malformed payload containers, injected tenant, undeclared count, integer confirmation, missing permission, changed payload under one idempotency key, changed-payload reconciliation, missing reconciliation operation, bounded uncertainty, nested cache isolation, and malformed output rollback. Every corrected rejection asserts that rooms, cache, and sequence remain unchanged where applicable. copy.deepcopy is the standard-library mechanism used to isolate nested state: https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.deepcopy.

Provider-neutral transfer: schemas, trusted-context separation, authorization order, idempotency, output validation, and postcondition checks remain server responsibilities regardless of model. Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai are optional model families that a deployment might use. Their schema adherence, tool calling, hosting, authentication, and transport capabilities are deployment-specific and are not assumed. The exercise remains independently testable offline.
The elapsed runtime is UNKNOWN until the files are executed on a particular machine. The deterministic runner intentionally omits timing so that the expected evidence remains exact.
sections.callout:
How to interpret the expected result:
All eight contract tests are expected to pass. The strict-schema regression is not an intentionally failing test and is not required to produce an error. It verifies the corrected boundary behavior by asserting ValueError for the injected tenant before the insecure service is called, then asserting that the insecure service's rooms remain unchanged.

sections.title: Eight contract tests
paragraphs: Save this complete file as test_contract.py. It preserves the seven existing passing tests and replaces the defective test_08 with a strict-schema regression. The replacement asserts ValueError for an injected tenant before the insecure service is called, then asserts that the insecure service state remains unchanged.

Exact expected output: PASS test_01_success_replay_and_single_effect; PASS test_02_uncertainty_reconciliation_and_missing_operation; PASS test_03_changed_payload_conflicts_in_reserve_and_reconcile; PASS test_04_insecure_variant_mutates_but_corrected_service_does_not; PASS test_05_malformed_extra_boolean_and_permission_rejections; PASS test_06_cached_nested_evidence_is_isolated; PASS test_07_invalid_output_rolls_back_all_state; PASS test_08_strict_schema_rejects_injected_tenant_before_insecure_mutation; SUMMARY tests=8 passed=8 failures=0 errors=0. Each semicolon represents a newline. The result format uses Python's standard unittest framework: https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html.

code.label: test_contract.py
code.code:
import copy
import sys
import unittest

from reserve_room import ROOM_ID, RoomService, SLOTS, validate_input
from wrong_schema_auth import InsecureSchemaOnlyService


def context():
    return {
        "identity": "user-ivy",
        "tenant": "tenant-cedar",
        "permissions": ["reserve:study-room"]
    }


def payload():
    return {
        "requested_slot": SLOTS[0],
        "request_id": "req-worked-1",
        "confirmation": True
    }


def snapshot(service):
    return copy.deepcopy((service.rooms, service.cache, service.sequence))


class ContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_01_success_replay_and_single_effect(self):
        service = RoomService()
        first = service.reserve(payload(), context())
        replay = service.reserve(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(first, replay)
        self.assertEqual(first["status"], "success")
        self.assertEqual(first["operation_id"], "op-0001")
        self.assertEqual(service.sequence, 1)
        self.assertEqual(service.rooms, {(ROOM_ID, SLOTS[0]): ("tenant-cedar", "user-ivy")})

    def test_02_uncertainty_reconciliation_and_missing_operation(self):
        service = RoomService()
        pending = service.reserve(payload(), context(), "uncertain")
        self.assertEqual(pending["status"], "pending")
        confirmed = service.reconcile(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(confirmed["status"], "success")
        self.assertEqual(confirmed["evidence"]["reconciliation_count"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(service.rooms), 1)

        missing_service = RoomService()
        before = snapshot(missing_service)
        missing = missing_service.reconcile(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(missing["reason"]["code"], "OPERATION_NOT_FOUND")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot(missing_service), before)

        bounded = RoomService()
        bounded.reserve(payload(), context(), "uncertain")
        bounded.rooms.clear()
        first_check = bounded.reconcile(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(first_check["status"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(first_check["evidence"]["reconciliation_count"], 1)
        bounded.rooms[(ROOM_ID, SLOTS[0])] = ("tenant-cedar", "user-ivy")
        second_check = bounded.reconcile(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(second_check["status"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(second_check["reason"]["code"], "RECONCILIATION_LIMIT")

    def test_03_changed_payload_conflicts_in_reserve_and_reconcile(self):
        service = RoomService()
        service.reserve(payload(), context(), "uncertain")
        changed = dict(payload(), requested_slot=SLOTS[1])
        before_rooms = copy.deepcopy(service.rooms)
        before_cache = copy.deepcopy(service.cache)
        reserve_result = service.reserve(changed, context())
        reconcile_result = service.reconcile(changed, context())
        self.assertEqual(reserve_result["reason"]["code"], "IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT")
        self.assertEqual(reconcile_result["reason"]["code"], "IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT")
        self.assertEqual(service.rooms, before_rooms)
        self.assertEqual(service.cache, before_cache)
        self.assertEqual(service.sequence, 1)

    def test_04_insecure_variant_mutates_but_corrected_service_does_not(self):
        forged = dict(payload(), tenant="tenant-maple")
        insecure = InsecureSchemaOnlyService()
        wrong_result = insecure.reserve(forged)
        self.assertEqual(wrong_result["tenant_used"], "tenant-maple")
        self.assertEqual(insecure.rooms[(ROOM_ID, SLOTS[0])], "tenant-maple")

        corrected = RoomService()
        before = snapshot(corrected)
        corrected_result = corrected.reserve(forged, context())
        self.assertEqual(corrected_result["status"], "denied")
        self.assertEqual(corrected_result["reason"]["code"], "BOUNDARY_REJECTED")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot(corrected), before)

    def test_05_malformed_extra_boolean_and_permission_rejections(self):
        service = RoomService()
        cases = [
            None,
            dict(payload(), count=1),
            dict(payload(), confirmation=1)
        ]
        for bad in cases:
            before = snapshot(service)
            self.assertEqual(service.reserve(bad, context())["status"], "denied")
            self.assertEqual(snapshot(service), before)
        no_permission = dict(context(), permissions=[])
        before = snapshot(service)
        result = service.reserve(payload(), no_permission)
        self.assertEqual(result["reason"]["code"], "PERMISSION_DENIED")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot(service), before)
        malformed_context = []
        before = snapshot(service)
        self.assertEqual(service.reserve(payload(), malformed_context)["status"], "denied")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot(service), before)

    def test_06_cached_nested_evidence_is_isolated(self):
        service = RoomService()
        first = service.reserve(payload(), context())
        first["evidence"]["tenant"] = "tenant-attacker"
        first["reason"]["message"] = "mutated by caller"
        replay = service.reserve(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(replay["evidence"]["tenant"], "tenant-cedar")
        self.assertEqual(replay["reason"]["message"], "reservation postcondition is confirmed")
        self.assertEqual(service.cache[("tenant-cedar", "user-ivy", "req-worked-1")]["result"], replay)

    def test_07_invalid_output_rolls_back_all_state(self):
        def remove_evidence(candidate):
            candidate.pop("evidence")
            return candidate

        service = RoomService(test_output_transform=remove_evidence)
        before = snapshot(service)
        result = service.reserve(payload(), context())
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "denied")
        self.assertEqual(result["reason"]["code"], "POSTCONDITION_UNVERIFIED")
        self.assertEqual(snapshot(service), before)

    def test_08_strict_schema_rejects_injected_tenant_before_insecure_mutation(self):
        insecure = InsecureSchemaOnlyService()
        forged = dict(payload(), tenant="tenant-maple")
        before = copy.deepcopy(insecure.rooms)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            ValueError,
            "INVALID_INPUT: exact input fields are required; injected trust fields are forbidden"
        ):
            validate_input(forged)
        self.assertEqual(insecure.rooms, before)


class DeterministicResult(unittest.TestResult):
    def addSuccess(self, test):
        super().addSuccess(test)
        print("PASS " + test._testMethodName)

    def addFailure(self, test, err):
        super().addFailure(test, err)
        print("FAIL " + test._testMethodName + ": " + err[0].__name__ + ": " + str(err[1]))

    def addError(self, test, err):
        super().addError(test, err)
        print("ERROR " + test._testMethodName + ": " + err[0].__name__ + ": " + str(err[1]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(ContractTests)
    result = DeterministicResult()
    suite.run(result)
    passed = result.testsRun - len(result.failures) - len(result.errors)
    print("SUMMARY tests={} passed={} failures={} errors={}".format(
        result.testsRun, passed, len(result.failures), len(result.errors)))
    sys.exit(0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1)

sections.title: Changed-input learner task and fixture
paragraphs: Learner task: use the same reserve_room.py implementation with this independent fixture. Both trusted tenant and requested slot differ from the worked case. Before running it, predict the operation ID, status, evidence tenant, evidence caller, room key, and owner tuple.

Then reserve once, retain request_id req-changed-1, change only requested_slot to 2026-10-05T09:00Z, and call reserve again. Assert conflict, reason code IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, one room entry, sequence equal to one, and byte-for-byte equivalent logical room and cache snapshots before and after the rejected call.

Traceable decision: tenant-maple is accepted only because it arrives in trusted context. The payload selects 10:00Z. A fresh service produces op-0001. The exact owner is tenant-maple and user-ivy. Changing the slot changes the digest while preserving the trusted idempotency key, so the second call conflicts without mutation.

sections.title: Changed-input complete solution and actionable feedback
paragraphs: Save this complete solution as test_changed_solution.py. Expected output is: PASS test_changed_tenant_and_slot; PASS test_same_key_changed_slot_is_conflict_and_immutable; SUMMARY tests=2 passed=2 failures=0 errors=0. Each semicolon represents a newline.

If tenant-maple is absent, verify that trusted context, rather than payload, supplies the tenant. If the slot is wrong, trace requested_slot from the changed fixture. If operation_id is not op-0001, start with a fresh RoomService. If the second result succeeds, verify that the digest covers the complete accepted payload. If state or sequence changes, ensure conflict handling returns before mutation.

code.label: test_changed_solution.py
code.code:
import copy
import json
import sys
import unittest

from reserve_room import ROOM_ID, RoomService


class ChangedInputSolution(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        with open("changed_fixture.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            self.fixture = json.load(handle)
        self.service = RoomService()

    def test_changed_tenant_and_slot(self):
        result = self.service.reserve(self.fixture["payload"], self.fixture["context"])
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "success")
        self.assertEqual(result["operation_id"], "op-0001")
        self.assertEqual(result["slot"], "2026-10-05T10:00Z")
        self.assertEqual(result["evidence"], {
            "reserved": True,
            "tenant": "tenant-maple",
            "caller": "user-ivy",
            "reconciliation_count": 0
        })
        self.assertEqual(self.service.rooms, {
            (ROOM_ID, "2026-10-05T10:00Z"): ("tenant-maple", "user-ivy")
        })

    def test_same_key_changed_slot_is_conflict_and_immutable(self):
        self.service.reserve(self.fixture["payload"], self.fixture["context"])
        rooms_before = copy.deepcopy(self.service.rooms)
        cache_before = copy.deepcopy(self.service.cache)
        sequence_before = self.service.sequence
        changed = dict(self.fixture["payload"], requested_slot="2026-10-05T09:00Z")
        result = self.service.reserve(changed, self.fixture["context"])
        self.assertEqual(result["status"], "conflict")
        self.assertEqual(result["reason"]["code"], "IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT")
        self.assertEqual(self.service.rooms, rooms_before)
        self.assertEqual(self.service.cache, cache_before)
        self.assertEqual(self.service.sequence, sequence_before)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.service.rooms), 1)


class DeterministicResult(unittest.TestResult):
    def addSuccess(self, test):
        super().addSuccess(test)
        print("PASS " + test._testMethodName)

    def addFailure(self, test, err):
        super().addFailure(test, err)
        print("FAIL " + test._testMethodName + ": " + err[0].__name__ + ": " + str(err[1]))

    def addError(self, test, err):
        super().addError(test, err)
        print("ERROR " + test._testMethodName + ": " + err[0].__name__ + ": " + str(err[1]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(ChangedInputSolution)
    result = DeterministicResult()
    suite.run(result)
    passed = result.testsRun - len(result.failures) - len(result.errors)
    print("SUMMARY tests={} passed={} failures={} errors={}".format(
        result.testsRun, passed, len(result.failures), len(result.errors)))
    sys.exit(0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1)

sections.title: Blank reusable contract template
paragraphs: Use this only after completing the worked case. Preserve this resource's original id, slug, title, metadata enums, section IDs, source URLs, publishers, and verification dates when revising the learning resource itself.

For a new capability, replace every bracketed field. Keep model payload separate from server-supplied identity, tenant, permissions, policy, and other trusted context. Validate containers and primitive values before indexing, membership checks, regular expressions, state access, or mutation.

Treat MCP annotations and equivalent provider hints as descriptive metadata rather than enforcement. Record which production guarantees remain UNKNOWN until verified for the selected transport, host, model family, identity provider, persistence layer, and concurrency design.
